newsitem.title: USA: Exxon, Qatar in talks to build plant - WSJ. [CORRECTED 09:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Exxon, Qatar in talks to build plant - WSJ. [CORRECTED 09:42 GMT]

text.p: Exxon Corp is negotiating with Qatar to build the industry's first plant that would make commercial quantities of liquid diesel fuel and other products from natural gas, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper said Exxon officials had confirmed to it that the company was talking with state-owned Qatar General Petroleum Corp to build a plant based on its technology.
It said the plant, which would cost more than $1 billion to build, would convert gas produced from the emirate's North field into liquid petroleum products.

The newspaper quoted Fritz Voigt, Exxon's vice president for international gas, as saying the two companies were evaluating the results of a feasibility study of applying Exxon's technology in the country.

It said the plant would carry a cost of about $24,000 a barrel of output and would produce 50,000 to 100,000 barrels a day of middle distillate products from 500 million to 1.0 billion cubic feet of gas per day.
Exxon was also considering using the same technology in Alaska where it has gas reserves, it added.
